summary: Queued requests routed to I/O-bound variant producing sustained p99 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (AcmeRetail, dedicated) reported elevated p99 across text-generation requests starting 2026-03-05 11:08 UTC. Root cause traced to requests queuing and being routed to a lower-cost I/O-optimized model variant that relies on memory-mapped weights. That variant experiences heavy page faults on first-activation under burst traffic, producing sustained p99 latency spikes (~4-8s) and intermittent 504s while cache warms.

Impact:
- Affected customer: AcmeRetail (dedicated) production traffic to model family gpt-j-6B.
- Symptom: sustained p99 latency from baseline ~220ms to 4s-8s for ~30-45 minutes. Intermittent 504 observed when router retried timed-out requests.
- Business impact: degraded UX for recommendation pipeline; increased error rate visible on customer's dashboard.

Environment/Context:
- Region: us-east-1 (prod).
- Traffic pattern: high concurrency spike during batch ingestion window (11:00-11:15 UTC).
- Routing policy: cost-aware fallback enabled (prefer compatible variants with lower memory footprint/cost).

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) In prod us-east, configure model route for gpt-j-6B with cost-preference and fallback to gpt-j-6B-quantized variant.
2) Drive a burst of ~120 concurrent streaming generation requests (prompt length ~512 tokens, seq_len request ~1024).
3) Observe routing decisions when primary warm pool saturates: requests diverted to low-memory quantized variant which is disk-backed on that rack.
4) Measure p99 on route and note sustained elevated latencies and occasional 504s during first 20-40 minutes.

Observed logs/metrics (snippets):
- router: "chosen_variant=gpt-j-6B-quantized reason=cost_preference primary_full=false"
- runtime: "pmem_page_faults=high replica_state=initializing mmap_load=true"
- api-gateway: "upstream_timeout=504 rt_p99=5.12s rt_p50=260ms"

Relevant links:
- Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/latency/acmeretail-gptj (p99 spike graph)
- Incident Slack: #support (thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02/support/p164)
- Post-incident runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/routing-fallbacks

Temporary mitigation requested by customer:
- Can we pin route to the higher-memory variant until warm pool scaling completes?
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-05T11:25Z): Customer reported sudden p99 spike; assigned to SRE. They observed retries and 504s in client's logs. Asked for immediate mitigation: pin route or increase reserved capacity.

Omar Patel (2026-03-05T11:42Z): Confirmed routing decisions show cost_preference path chosen after warm pool filled. Initial hypothesis: fallback routing allowed io-bound quantized variant to accept traffic before it was pre-warmed, causing mmap page-fault storm.

SRE Team (2026-03-05T12:05Z): Temporary action: adjusted routing weights to prefer fp16 warm replicas in us-east for AcmeRetail's route and triggered pre-warm for two additional quantized replicas. Observed p99 drop to ~350ms within 18 minutes.
AcmeRetail Ops (2026-03-05T12:50Z): Confirming UX improvements; error-rate returned to normal. Customer requests PSA about cost-aware fallback behavior to avoid future surprises.
Omar Patel (2026-03-07T09:15Z): Postmortem draft up on Confluence, proposing changes to routing policy and pre-warm thresholds. Linked PRs to follow for router/gating changes.
investigation_notes: 11:10 UTC - examined router decision logs: cost_preference policy returned variant with lower memory footprint but higher cold-activation I/O profile.
11:20 UTC - runtime traces show heavy pmem page faults and long mmap read times; kernel-level stalls observed on replica nodes hosting quantized variants.
11:35 UTC - correlated traffic surge with warm-pool exhaustion; primary warm replicas hit max concurrency and router allowed fallback activation under 'allow-warmup' flag.

Hypothesis: Combination of (1) aggressive cost_preference routing, (2) allow-warmup=true, and (3) insufficient pre-warm threshold for quantized replicas caused immediate activation of io-bound replicas under load, producing page fault storms and long p99s.
Checked related PRs for scheduler autoscale behavior: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/88 (recent change to pre-warm threshold).
resolution:
Mitigations applied 2026-03-05 12:10 UTC: 1) Temporarily adjusted routing weights to prefer in-memory fp16 replicas for AcmeRetail; 2) Forced pre-warm of two additional quantized replicas on us-east rack; 3) Updated router config to block activation of disk-backed variants under high-concurrency bursts (introduce activation_cooldown).
Permanent changes (deployed 2026-03-07): 1) Router: conservative cost_preference when warm_pool_utilization > 80%; 2) Scheduler: increased default pre-warm threshold for quantized variants and added telemetry to detect high page-fault rates; 3) Added documentation and alerting rule for 'mmap page-fault storm'.
Outcome: p99 returned to expected range and error-rate normalized. No further customer complaints after fixes rolled out.
follow_up_tasks: ROUTER-210: Add activation_cooldown config and conservative routing option when warm_pool > 80%
SCHEDULER-145: Increase pre-warm threshold for quantized/disk-backed variants and add auto-prewarm on surge
DOCS-54: Update public docs and support KB about cost-aware fallback behavior and recommendations for dedicated customers
ENG-OPS: Run chaos test to simulate warm-pool exhaustion and validate new gating rules (owner: Omar Patel)
